title: Rita Demetri and the Harlem Song and Dance tour of France
summary: Recent work with Rita Demetri and a one-nighter tour in France in 1976.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, we've talked about your involvement with shows and accompanying people, et cetera, et cetera, which more or less brings us up to the, you know, the present time. I know I had lost, kind of lost contact with you because I think you were doing so many of these, you know, backing jobs for singers and all that, and I remember, you know, seeing your name in connection with Rita Demetri.
Now, when did that start? Just a couple years ago?
Couple years ago, uh-huh, with Wayne Wright, the two of us and her husband, Stanley Graves, played the piano. I worked there several months until I went to France.
Yeah, well, what were you doing in France?
I was there on tour with a group called the Harlem Song and Dance.
Well, it was an old Apollo type sort of
situation, and Billy Butler was one of the guitarists, and Milton Larkins and Carrie Smith and a very fine dancer. I can't recall his name right this minute. I should. And --
Yes, Jimmy Sly, Jimmy Sly, the tap dancer. And Ram Ramirez and Eddy Locke and myself. And we did one-nighters from one end of France to the other.
